document.title: Self-Hosted iOS Development, Signing, Sideloading, Distribution, and Provisioning-Refresh Handoff
document.scope: Complete record of the proposed zero-cost, non-jailbroken, privately hosted iOS development and distribution architecture discussed in this conversation.

executive_summary.goal: Build a privately hosted iOS development and distribution system that allows the owner to develop apps, automatically build and sign them, publish IPAs on infrastructure they control, and minimize or automate Apple's free Personal Team provisioning refresh requirements.
executive_summary.primary_constraint: The owner does not want to pay Apple the $99/year Apple Developer Program fee.
secondary_constraints: Automate as much of the process as possible.

recommended_architecture.source_control: Self-hosted Git or existing Git provider
recommended_architecture.IPA_repository: Private HTTPS service accessible through Tailscale
recommended_architecture.iOS_distribution_client: AltStore Classic or another compatible sideload/refresh mechanism

executive_summary.core_principle: Do not attempt to defeat Apple's cryptographic signing or provisioning system. Instead, automate the legitimate free Personal Team workflow and accept its limits.
executive_summary.most_important_caveat: A free Personal Team provisioning profile has a short validity period. Infrastructure can automate refresh/rebuild/reinstallation, but it cannot turn a free Apple development identity into a permanent unrestricted signing identity.

conversation_context.original_question: Can an IPA package be downloaded and installed on an iPhone?
conversation_context.clarification: The user was specifically interested in which installation/distribution methods are free to the developer.
conversation_context.developer_goal: Write and distribute iOS applications without paying Apple $99/year.
conversation_context.distribution_target: Potentially 5-20 friends, although personal/self-owned device deployment is the primary architectural target.
regional_context: User has friends in the EU.
User can potentially access those friends' addresses.
User uses a VPN and can select different apparent network locations.
conversation_context.important_regional_conclusion: A VPN or merely having a friend's address does not automatically establish eligibility for Apple's regional alternative-distribution programs. Physical/device/account eligibility must be treated separately from IP geolocation.

hardware_context.networking: Tailscale is already available and is embedded in at least one of the user's applications.

overview.developer_cost: $0 when using a free Apple development identity

free_personal_team.purpose: Apple's free development provisioning for personal development/testing.
free_personal_team.operational_effect: The application may stop launching when its provisioning expires unless it has been refreshed/reinstalled with valid provisioning.
free_personal_team.important_distinction: A sideloading application can automate or simplify refreshing, but it does not eliminate Apple's underlying provisioning validity.

seven_day_issue.user_reaction: The user considers the 7-day expiration unacceptable/stupid.
seven_day_issue.technical_reality: The expiration is an Apple-imposed provisioning constraint.
seven_day_issue.important_response: The system should automate the maintenance rather than attempt to defeat the expiration.

desired_user_experience.manual: Install -> wait 7 days -> app expires -> manually reinstall
desired_user_experience.desired: Install -> infrastructure monitors provisioning -> refresh/rebuild before expiration -> app remains usable with minimal manual intervention

seven_day_issue.hard_boundary: The automation does not create permanent free provisioning.
seven_day_issue.design_goal: Make the 7-day restriction operationally invisible or nearly invisible where technically possible.

third_party_sideloading.general_model: These tools automate some or all of the signing, installation, and refresh workflow while still depending on Apple's provisioning/signing infrastructure.
third_party_sideloading.security_warning: Do not give Apple credentials to arbitrary third-party signing services merely because they promise permanent or unlimited signing.
third_party_sideloading.preferred_security_model: Perform signing locally on owned hardware where possible.
third_party_sideloading.reason: The user owns multiple Macs and an always-on Mac mini, so there is little reason to outsource Apple credential handling to an unknown service.

AltSign.function: Provides functionality used by AltServer-related workflows to interact with Apple's signing infrastructure.

altstore_architecture.important_design_choice: Use AltStore-compatible source metadata rather than inventing a proprietary IPA catalog protocol unless a custom client is eventually required.

self_hosting_strategy.question_addressed: How to duplicate AltStore/AltServer-like behavior on infrastructure controlled by the user?
self_hosting_strategy.answer: Split the problem into build/signing, artifact hosting, device installation/refresh, and orchestration rather than trying to reproduce the entire system as one server.

recommended_split.Apple_signing: Mac mini using Xcode and Apple development identity

self_hosting_strategy.reason: Apple-specific operations naturally belong on macOS; generic infrastructure is better handled by Linux.

reason_not_primary: The Mac mini is always on.
Xcode is Apple's native build/signing environment.
There is no need to recreate Apple's signing behavior if Xcode can perform it.
community_implementations: AltServer-Linux and related projects demonstrate that portions of AltServer functionality can be implemented outside macOS.
why_not_a_linux_signing_server.recommendation: Do not make Linux responsible for Apple signing unless a later requirement makes that necessary.

why_it_is_ideal: Already participates in the NAS environment
Can access the iPhone when appropriate
Can act as a persistent build/signing worker
mac_mini_role.security_boundary: Treat the Mac mini as a privileged Apple credential/signing host.

macbook_role.recommended_workflow: Developer works interactively on MacBook Pro and pushes code to source control; CI then builds the app on the Mac mini.

do_not_store: Apple authentication tokens unless absolutely required
linux_vm_role.reason: Keep the Apple credential trust boundary on macOS.

nas_role.purpose: Persistent storage for build and release artifacts.

tailscale_architecture.user_context: The user already uses Tailscale and has Tailscale embedded in their application.

important_distinction.statement: Application-level Tailscale functionality and system-level Tailscale connectivity on iOS should not be assumed to be equivalent.
important_distinction.consequence: An installation/refresh manager cannot necessarily use the private network path created by the user's application.
important_distinction.recommended: Use the standard/system Tailscale iOS network path when the installation manager itself must access the tailnet.

security: Restrict repository access to trusted devices.
Do not expose signing services to the public Internet.
Use HTTPS where practical even inside the tailnet.

no_domain_required.reason: Tailscale provides private connectivity and naming within the tailnet.

source_json.note: The exact schema must be generated according to the current AltStore source specification rather than relying on this conceptual example.

build_pipeline.desired_user_experience: git push -> automated build -> signed IPA -> private repository -> iPhone installation/update

pipeline.name: CI trigger
pipeline.action: Detect new commit and queue build.

pipeline.name: Mac dispatch
pipeline.action: Send build request to Mac mini.

pipeline.name: Dependency resolution
pipeline.action: Resolve Swift Package Manager, CocoaPods, or other dependencies as applicable.

pipeline.name: Signing/export
pipeline.action: Sign and export IPA using permitted Apple development provisioning.

pipeline.name: Validation
pipeline.action: Inspect IPA, bundle identifier, version, build number, entitlements, and provisioning expiration.

pipeline.name: Publication
pipeline.action: Publish immutable IPA and update source metadata.

pipeline.name: Notification
pipeline.action: Report build result and provisioning expiration.

conceptual_commands.archive: xcodebuild -project MyApp.xcodeproj -scheme MyApp -configuration Release -archivePath build/MyApp.xcarchive archive

xcode_automation.important_note: These are conceptual commands. Actual signing, export options, workspace/project configuration, bundle identifiers, capabilities, and provisioning settings must be adapted to the specific application.
xcode_automation.preferred_signing: Use Xcode's legitimate Apple signing workflow wherever practical.

signing_architecture.principle: The Mac mini is the Apple signing trust boundary.
reason: Xcode is Apple's native development environment.
No need to reimplement Apple's signing protocol unnecessarily.
signing_architecture.linux_role: Request and monitor builds, but do not require direct Apple credential access.
signing_architecture.hard_limit: Self-hosting cannot manufacture an unrestricted Apple signing identity.

refresh_architecture.objective: Make the free Personal Team's short provisioning lifetime as invisible as possible.
operational_strategy: Refresh while the device and required services are reachable.
If refresh cannot occur, notify the owner.
Never assume that automated refresh removes Apple's underlying expiration.

tailscale.caveat: The refresh mechanism may have additional requirements beyond ordinary HTTP connectivity.

rules: Apple credentials stay on Mac mini.
CI should not receive Apple passwords.
Back up source and release artifacts.

important_conclusion.vpn: Changing VPN exit location does not by itself establish regional eligibility.
important_conclusion.address: Using a friend's address does not by itself establish eligibility.
important_conclusion.device: Physical/device location and regional eligibility can also matter.
important_conclusion.recommendation: Do not attempt to fabricate regional eligibility merely to avoid the Developer Program fee.

alternative_distribution.limitation: Regional alternative distribution is not equivalent to a universal free IPA sideloading mechanism.
alternative_distribution.recommendation: Treat as a separate future investigation, not as the foundation of this architecture.

five_to_twenty_friends.question: Can 5-20 friends receive the app for free without the $99 Apple Developer Program?
five_to_twenty_friends.answer: Not through Apple's normal unrestricted distribution mechanisms using a free Personal Team.

alternative_distribution.fit: Potentially relevant for eligible regional users/developers
alternative_distribution.limitation: Does not turn a U.S. free Personal Team into unrestricted worldwide distribution.

self_hosted_server_design.question: Can AltStore/AltServer behavior be duplicated on self-owned servers?
self_hosted_server_design.answer: Much of the infrastructure can be self-hosted, but Apple's signing/provisioning authority remains external.
self_hosted_server_design.recommended_model: Self-host everything except the Apple-controlled signing/provisioning operations.

potential_custom_architecture.diagram: Developer MacBook -> Linux CI -> Mac mini -> Xcode/Apple signing -> NAS/private IPA repository -> Tailscale -> iPhone

potential_custom_ios_client.reason: AltStore already solves much of the iOS-side management problem.
build_only_if: AltServer refresh behavior cannot meet requirements.
The user wants a custom private app-management UX.
A fully self-contained product is desired.
potential_custom_ios_client.risk: Maintaining iOS-specific installation and signing compatibility is substantially more work than hosting IPAs.

security: Verify public Internet cannot reach repository.
Verify unauthorized tailnet devices cannot access repository.
Verify Linux CI cannot retrieve Apple credentials.

security_do_not_do: Do not put Apple passwords in Git.
Do not put Apple passwords in plaintext CI configuration.
Do not expose Apple authentication services publicly.
Do not expose the IPA repository publicly unless explicitly required.
Do not trust arbitrary third-party signing services with Apple credentials.
Do not attempt to cryptographically bypass provisioning expiration.
Do not assume a VPN IP address creates regional eligibility.
Do not falsify Apple Account country/region information solely to bypass regional rules.

decision_log.reason: User explicitly wants a $0 development/distribution workflow.
Only practical official zero-cost Apple development identity.

decision_log.decision: Automate the 7-day maintenance rather than bypass it.
decision_log.reason: Provisioning validity is controlled by Apple.

decision_log.decision: Use Mac mini for Apple-specific operations.
decision_log.reason: Always-on and capable of running Xcode.

decision_log.decision: Use Linux VMs for generic infrastructure.
decision_log.reason: Excellent for CI, Git, monitoring, APIs, and orchestration.

decision_log.decision: Use NAS for persistent IPA artifacts.
Use Tailscale rather than public Internet.
decision_log.reason: Already available and eliminates need for public DNS/domain/port forwarding.
Avoid unnecessary reinvention of the iOS installation layer.

decision_log.decision: Keep Apple credentials on Mac mini.

alternative_architectures_considered.reason: Unnecessary because user owns Macs and uses Tailscale.
Credential/security concerns and unnecessary given owned Macs.
Regional eligibility is more than VPN/IP/address and should not be fabricated.

recommended_end_state.developer_experience: Push code from MacBook Pro and let infrastructure build/publish it automatically.
recommended_end_state.manual_intervention: Only when Apple's free provisioning/authentication/device constraints require it.
recommended_end_state.ultimate_limitation: Apple's free Personal Team provisioning rules.

when_to_pay_apple: Manual free-provisioning maintenance becomes more annoying than $99/year.
future_upgrade_path.benefit: The architecture does not need to be thrown away. The Mac mini build/signing pipeline and private artifact repository can remain useful even after joining the paid program.

open_questions: Which exact iPhone model and iOS version will be the primary target?
Which macOS version is running on the Mac mini?
Is the Mac mini Apple Silicon or Intel?

Does the user need remote refresh while the iPhone is away from the home LAN?

recommended_next_action.description: Build a minimal end-to-end proof of concept before implementing the full CI system.
steps: 1. Confirm the Mac mini's macOS and Xcode versions.
2. Sign into Xcode with the normal Apple Account.
4. Install it on the primary iPhone using Personal Team signing.
5. Inspect the generated provisioning profile and expiration.
6. Install and configure the chosen AltStore/refresh mechanism.
7. Confirm that the iPhone can reach a private Tailscale-hosted HTTP/HTTPS repository.
8. Publish a test IPA and source catalog.
9. Install the IPA through the chosen mechanism.
11. Only after that works, implement Linux CI and automated xcodebuild.

final_architecture_statement: The preferred solution is a completely private, self-hosted iOS build and sideload infrastructure in which Linux handles generic CI/orchestration, the always-on Mac mini handles Xcode and Apple's legitimate signing/provisioning operations, the NAS stores immutable IPAs and build artifacts, Tailscale provides private connectivity without a public domain or public server, and AltStore/AltServer or a compatible mechanism handles iOS-side installation and refresh. The system should automate Apple's free provisioning workflow rather than attempting to bypass Apple's signing or expiration controls.
